## D — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
Accuracy scope: Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops; each fact block identifies exactly one registered physical source page.
Dated crash totals, current compact membership exceptions, broad drug-legality statements and questionable absorption or elimination generalizations are held as source debt. Alcohol examples are identified as handbook examples, not safe-driving thresholds. The handbook's low-BAC reassurance conflicts with its subsequent risk warning. Traffic-stop search language is preserved with the stated probable-cause condition and source-currency debt.
The author completed a semantic source-fidelity pass over every drafted fact before submission; the scratch receipts enumerate every fact identifier and verdict. This is same-model work and independent coverage and hallucination review remain pending.
Shared pages contribute noncommercial material only. Unreadable graphics are withheld; no picture-dependent rule has been reconstructed from memory.
Currency warning: applicability of the issuer-linked older edition remains source debt (verify WY-SEC06-FRESH).

corpus_stability.reason: Single issuer-linked edition is staged; this is an operational corpus classification, not a verified update frequency or present legal currency. The current issuer warning is retained as source freshness debt in A and D.

verification_debt.claim_text: The issuer warns printed manual material can be outdated; refresh before asserting present-day legal applicability.
The current compact membership exceptions listed on physical page 33 are edition-sensitive and have not been independently refreshed.
Undated annual fatality totals and proportions on physical page 33 cannot establish current crash statistics.

Physical page 34 gives broad absorption, food-delay, liver-elimination and constant drink-per-hour generalizations; exact numeric clearance rules are withheld pending current authoritative support and must never become a safe-to-drive timer.
Physical page 34 says low BAC affects most persons insignificantly, while page 35 describes increased crash risk at that level; no reassuring low-BAC threshold is taught.
The broad drug-illegality sentence on physical page 38 is not used to establish present-day legal status; current legal classification requires official verification.
